text.actionPlaceholder: What changes the cause or the control

S.name: Severity
S.question: How bad is the effect for the customer or the people when the failure happens?
levels: A slight inconvenience that few notice.
A small inconvenience that most notice; no rework.
A little rework or a short delay inside the shift.
Rework or a late order; the customer notices.
A damaged or incomplete delivery; complaint and re-send.
The process stops or needs heavy rework; a customer may be lost.
The service fails for many customers at once.
Safety or regulatory breach that announces itself first.
Injury or regulatory breach with no warning at all.

O.name: Occurrence
O.question: How often does this cause lead to the failure, with the process as it runs today?
levels: Practically ruled out; nobody has seen it.
Happens nearly every time the step runs.

D.name: Detection
D.question: How likely is it that today's controls catch the failure before it reaches the customer?
levels: The step cannot pass the error; it is blocked at source.
An automatic check at the step catches it every time.
An automatic check at a later step catches it.
A second person checks it at the step.
The operator checks it by eye at the step.
A visual check at a later step, or a sample check.
Found only by chance or in an audit.
Found only after the process, by the next department.
No control; it is never found, or found too late.

steps: Picking
Right item, right quantity, right tote
Packing
Right box, fill and label; parcel closed and scanned
Loading
Stable wall in the right trailer; doors closed on time

templates.process: Front office: check-in to night audit
steps: Check-in
Guest identified, right room and rate, keys handed over
Payment guarantee
Card authorised or deposit taken for every stay
Posting
Every charge on the right folio on the right day

templates.name: Delivery route
templates.process: Last mile: load, drive, hand over, return
steps: Loading the van
Parcels in stop order, each scanned to the vehicle
Driving to the stop
Right address, planned sequence, safe driving
Handover at the door
Right parcel to the right person, with proof of delivery
Return to depot
Undelivered parcels scanned back with a reason

H.meaning: Action priority high: the team must find an action that lowers occurrence or improves detection, or document why it cannot. Severity rarely changes; the cause and the controls do.
moves: Agree one action with one owner and a date this week; a wish without an owner is not an action.
Prefer a change that stops the cause (prevention) over one that finds the failure later (detection).
When the action is done, rate S, O and D again on the same row and compare the RPN.
H.question: What would have to be true at this step for this failure to become impossible?

M.meaning: Action priority medium: the team should find an action; if none is worth it, write down why the risk is accepted, with the controls that keep it where it is.
moves: Check the detection control first: a cheap check at the step often moves D by several points.
Give the action an owner and a date, or record the decision to accept the risk.
Re-rate after the action; a medium that turns low frees the team for the next one.
M.question: Which control do we trust here, and when did we last see it work?

L.meaning: Action priority low: no action is required. Keep the controls that are there and review the row when the process changes.
moves: Keep the prevention and detection controls in the standard work.
Review the rating when volume, staff or layout change.
Spend the team's time on the high and medium rows first.
L.question: Which control holds this risk low, and is it still in place today?

rows.cause: Heavy parcels stacked on light ones at peak
rows.prevention: Stacking standard on the dock wall
rows.detection: None until the delivery station scans the damage
rows.action: Heavy-first zone at the dock and a wall check before the doors close

rows.cause: Two labels printed in a row and picked up out of order
rows.prevention: Print on demand at the pack station
rows.action: Printer releases the label only after the parcel scan

rows.cause: Empty slot at the location; the picker skips it
rows.action: A short pick needs a reason code; it cannot be skipped

rows.function: Trolley at the pack line by wave time
rows.effect: Idle pack station, late wave, missed cut-off
rows.cause: Only one lift free at peak
rows.detection: Supervisor sees the gap on the floor
rows.action: Second lift key and a trolley runner from 20:00

rows.cause: Right box size not at the station
rows.action: Box size per item group printed on the pack list

rows.function: Doors closed and sealed on time
rows.mode: Trailer leaves without the last cage
rows.effect: Parcels left on the dock, late delivery
rows.cause: Loader not told the cage count
rows.prevention: Cage count on the load sheet
rows.detection: Dispatcher checks the sheet before release
rows.action: Load sheet signed by loader and dispatcher

rows.mode: Pallet jack hits a loader's foot
rows.cause: Trolleys parked in the narrow dock lane
rows.action: Taped trolley parking zone; no trolley in the lane

rows.effect: Parcel invisible, missed cut-off, customer not informed

rows.cause: Fragile flag missing in the system
rows.action: Flag the 50 most fragile SKUs this week

rows.mode: Manifest closed after the trailer left
rows.effect: Parcels not traceable for a day
rows.cause: Dispatcher handles two doors at peak
rows.detection: System alert when departure precedes the manifest

rows.mode: Cage not locked in the trailer
rows.effect: Cage rolls, parcels crushed, loader hurt
rows.cause: Lock bar missing in some trailers
rows.action: Trailers without a lock bar are refused at the door

tips: Rate the cause, not the person.
Occurrence is how often the cause leads to the failure with the process as it runs today, whoever is on shift.
Rate the chance that what you have now catches it before the customer, not the check you plan to add.
Two rows with the same RPN can need different urgency: a severity 9 with a low occurrence still gets an action. Read the AP first, the RPN second.
That is the point of the sheet: when the action is done, rate S, O and D again on the same row and see what the risk is now.
